subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should `chat.send` return `started` only after the WebChat user turn is durably recorded or otherwise guaranteed to progress, or should delayed runtime-owned persistence remain the contract with UI-only pending protection?
rationale: The remaining fix changes a core Gateway/session behavior boundary rather than a simple UI race, and the existing candidate PR shows the persistence ownership, duplicate-suppression, and rollover tradeoffs need maintainer intent.

options.title: Durable Before ACK
options.body: Require `chat.send` to persist or otherwise prove the user turn is recoverable/progressing before returning `started`, using the shared recorder/session writer boundary.

options.title: Keep Delayed Runtime Persistence
options.body: Treat the current UI pending-send preservation as sufficient and accept that `started` does not imply durable transcript visibility.

options.title: Replace The Candidate PR
options.body: Close or supersede the broad open PR with a narrower gateway recorder change that proves busy-session, rollover, media, hooks, and failure paths.

recommendation.title: Durable Before ACK
recommendation.body: Require `chat.send` to persist or otherwise prove the user turn is recoverable/progressing before returning `started`, using the shared recorder/session writer boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session transcript maintenance plus likely authority over the Gateway/session product contract make this the best available routing owner from the observed history.
